title: A completed smooth section chart and a generic point of the original closed fibre
statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $\varphi:A\to B$ a flat local homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $q:L\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Suppose $s:\operatorname{Spec}B\to L$ lies over $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exist $n\geq0$ and a flat morphism $t:\operatorname{Spec}(B[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]])\to L$ [def-weil-flat-morphism] commuting with the maps to $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Evaluation of the variables at zero induces an origin point over the closed point of $B$; its image under $t$ equals the image of that closed point under $s$. There are a point $v$ of this power-series spectrum whose prime ideal is $\mathfrak m_B B[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$, a point $\eta$ of the closed fibre of $q$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and a nonempty open $W$ in that fibre [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], such that $t(v)$ is the image of $\eta$ and $\eta$ specializes to every point of $W$. Specialization means containment in the closure of the singleton.

proof.text: Lift the given map s to a section s-prime of the smooth base change pullback(q, Spec phi) over Spec B, using the supplied commuting square. Apply the smooth-section completion-chart lemma to obtain n and a flat t-prime compatible with the structure map and the entire section.

Spec phi is flat by hflat. Thus its base-change projection to L is flat, and composing with t-prime gives the desired flat t. The pullback condition and the chart structure-map equality give the commuting square. Compose the equality of entire section morphisms with the other pullback projection and evaluate at the closed point of B to obtain the origin equality.

Apply the generic-image lemma to the flat chart t-prime over the base-changed scheme. Obtain v with the prescribed extended maximal ideal and an affine open V in the original closed fibre, with x in V whose singleton closure is a component, and whose image is t(v).

The smooth closed fibre is locally Noetherian, so V is Noetherian. Use Mathlib NoetherianSpace.exists_isOpen_nonempty_subset_irreducibleComponent (Stacks 0052(3)) to obtain a nonempty open W inside closure {x} in V. Its image under the open immersion V to the fibre is open and nonempty. Membership in closure {x} gives specialization from x, and continuity of the immersion maps this to specialization from eta=V.ι(x).

theorem exists_smooth_section_power_series_chart
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    {L : Scheme.{u}} (q : L ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Smooth q]
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    (φ : A →+* B) [IsLocalHom φ] (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (s : Spec (.of B) ⟶ L) (hs : s ≫ q = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (t : Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) B)) ⟶ L), Flat t ∧
      t ≫ q = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.C (σ := Fin n))) ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ) ∧
      t ((Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (MvPowerSeries.constantCoeff (σ := Fin n))))
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint B)) = s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint B) ∧
      ∃ (v : Spec (.of (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) B)))
        (η : q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A))
        (W : (q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A)).Opens),
        v.asIdeal = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).map (MvPowerSeries.C (σ := Fin n)) ∧
        t v = q.fiberι (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) η ∧
        (W : Set (q.fiber (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A))).Nonempty ∧ ∀ z ∈ W, η ⤳ z
